findings.diagnosis: Three separate claims went: that machines took over work the body used to do, that a material free technology is the relevant kind in a constrained world, and that the shortage of attention is self imposed. The third is the volume’s premise about why any of this is available to an ordinary reader. What survives states the same fact about devices while dropping every reason it matters.

openQuestions.question:
Structural restoration blocked on route adjudication. This section is a chapter-start region: its prose sits between a part or container label and the first chapter heading beneath it, and text in that position compiles into a section with its own public route. Expanding it revives or reshapes a retired route, which is a continuity decision rather than an editorial one. The prose is therefore left exactly as it stood and the findings below describe what the prior pass removed rather than what this pass restored. The baseline text for this region is reproduced verbatim below so the author can restore it in one edit once the route decision is made. Punctuation repair under R-PUNCT-STRUCT is still required on it, and every ledger constraint named in this record still applies to it.

BASELINE TEXT:

*Presence, Presencing, and the Genius Between*

We are accustomed, in this age, to think of technology as something we construct outside ourselves — an apparatus, a device, a tool fashioned from the world to extend our reach into it. There is no quarrel here with any of it. But there is an older technology, and a more intimate one, which this work means to recover — for a great deal of what we now ask machines to do for us was once done, and can be done again, within. By technology we mean only what the word means: a disciplined know-how by which a capacity is reliably produced. An internal technology, then, is that know-how turned inward — a craft by which a state of being, a quality of perception, a manner of relation is reliably produced in oneself and drawn out in another. Its singular virtue, in an age straining the limits of the world’s material generosity, is that it requires no material at all. Its only raw resources are attention and care, of which there is no shortage but the one we impose upon ourselves.
